answer: A staked-identity ledge requires each agent to lock a bond sized to its claimed trust level, so spawning many identities costs proportionally more capital than one. Like a glacier slowly exposing fresh rock, reputation accrues only through verified transactions, making aged identities expensive to mass-produce. A hollow new identity with no history faces strict rate limits and escrow, so an attacker must fund and mature thousands of bonds, a cost that scales linearly and caps sybil gain.
